Hi everyone! I'm Syed Kamil Taqi Zaidi, a university student from Lahore, Pakistan, with a strong interest in space exploration, technology, innovation, and creative problem-solving.

I'm excited to participate in the NASA Space Apps Challenge because I love exploring new ideas and turning them into practical projects. I'm particularly interested in developing interactive and educational experiences that make complex scientific concepts easier and more enjoyable to understand.
summary:
# Planet X – SPHEREx Observatory

Planet X – SPHEREx Observatory is an interactive, AI-powered 3D space exploration platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It combines immersive astronomical visualization, artificial intelligence, and scientific data services to make space exploration more accessible, engaging, and educational.

The project features an interactive 3D solar system where users can explore planets and celestial objects, navigate the observatory, and experience simulated planetary close-up views. It also includes an immersive Andromeda Galaxy exploration experience featuring a procedurally generated star field with 1,800 individually selectable stars, each with different visual properties and stellar classifications.

At the heart of the platform is SpaceMind, an AI-powered scientific research assistant. It helps users investigate astronomical topics, understand selected celestial objects, discover scientific papers, and access connected space-science data services.

The platform also provides access to information about near-Earth asteroids, solar activity, planetary positions, telescope observations, exoplanets, and upcoming launches through its scientific data integrations.

Our goal is to bring 3D visualization, AI-assisted scientific learning, and real scientific resources together in one digital observatory. By transforming space science from passive reading into interactive exploration  and help users better understand our universe.
details:
Project Details

What the Project Does

Planet X – SPHEREx Observatory is a browser-based interactive space exploration platform. It allows users to explore astronomical environments in 3D, interact with celestial objects, and use an AI-powered assistant to learn about space science.

The project combines two major components:

1. Planet X – SPHEREx Frontend

The frontend provides the interactive observatory experience, including:

  • Interactive 3D solar-system visualization.
  • Planet and celestial-object selection.
  • Camera navigation and animated astronomical scenes.
  • Andromeda Galaxy exploration with a procedural field of 1,800 generated stars.
  • Individual star selection and contextual explanations.
  • Simulated planetary landing and close-approach views.
  • An integrated SpaceMind chat interface.

The Andromeda star field is a procedural educational visualization. Its generated stars are not presented as individually confirmed astronomical observations.

2. SpaceMind – AI Research and Scientific Backend

SpaceMind provides the research and data capabilities behind the observatory, including:

  • AI-powered astronomy research assistance.
  • Contextual explanations of celestial objects.
  • Scientific paper discovery and research retrieval.
  • Source-aware answers and citations.
  • NASA and other scientific data-provider integrations.
  • Supabase authentication, database services, and Edge Functions.
  • Scientific tools for astronomy and space-related calculations.

How It Works

The frontend uses JavaScript and Three.js to create the interactive 3D environment. Users can navigate the observatory, select celestial objects, and request explanations.

The Planet X interface communicates with SpaceMind through backend services. Supabase Edge Functions handle research requests and scientific data retrieval, while external providers supply relevant astronomical information.

The AI research system processes questions and uses connected research and data services to produce explanations. Scientific information is retrieved on demand rather than continuously streamed.

Benefits

  • Makes astronomy more accessible through interactive visualization.
  • Encourages curiosity and independent scientific learning.
  • Combines AI explanations with scientific resources.
  • Helps users explore celestial objects in an engaging environment.
  • Provides a foundation for future astronomy education and research applications.

Project Goals

Our goal is to develop a digital observatory that combines immersive space exploration, AI-powered research, and scientific data access in one platform.

We aim to make complex astronomical concepts easier to understand while encouraging users to explore reliable scientific resources.

Technologies and Programming Languages

  • HTML – Application structure.
  • CSS – Interface design and styling.
  • JavaScript – Application logic and interaction.
  • Three.js – 3D rendering and astronomical visualization.
  • Supabase – Authentication, database, and serverless Edge Functions.
  • Vercel – Application deployment and hosting.
  • GitHub – Source-code management and collaboration.
  • Groq – Hosted AI model provider used by the SpaceMind research backend.
  • Tavily and Semantic Scholar – Connected web research and scientific paper services.
  • python for Spacemind ( setting python libraries and python workspace)

The project uses a frontend/backend architecture with separate repositories for the observatory and SpaceMind research platform.
